description:
Source: docs/research/handwired.md (branch defk-snm/handwired-research; the numbers are in its stage 1, 1b and 2 sections) and the scripts bench/handwired_search.exs, bench/handwired_classes.exs, bench/handwired_f32.exs. AGENTS.md: record what a workload teaches about speed, including what did not help, with numbers, conditions (mark loaded runs provisional) and the source.

Entries for docs/performance.md (section 2, fast Elixir on binaries, or 1.x for the measuring lessons; follow "How to read an entry"):
- Anchor, then verify. :binary.matches/2 finds a literal anchor byte ('-', '.', '_') and Elixir checks the bytes around it. For date, float and snake-case patterns over 100k JSON documents it beat :re and a defk bit-parallel NFA by 1.5 to 2 times (12 chunks: 7.2 to 9.6 ms against 14.2 to 14.9 ms for defk, 19 to 26 ms for :re).
- Literal search: :binary.matches/3 with a scope on one packed blob, in 12 chunks, matched a defk shift-and kernel (6.8 to 8.6 ms against 9.2 to 9.5 ms). Elixir is the answer for literals.
- A backtracking spelling, ([a-z]+)+x, took 8 times as long as [a-z]+x in :re. Write the simple form first.
- defk's NFA costs about 3.2 ns per byte whatever the pattern (18 helper calls per byte); it wins only where no literal anchor exists.
- Exact float32 through an [f32] scratch write is free (0.91x the f64 time) and 60x faster than rounding with <<v::float-32>> in Elixir; the 5.5x gap to C float in one thread is the runtime checks (see the check-elimination ticket).
Also: a short evidence note in docs/scope.md (or docs/research/nx-boundary.md) that for this workload the best CPU times (7 to 15 ms in 12 chunks) are in the range of handwired's WebGPU search (4.5 to 5.2 ms, the author's machine, an order of magnitude only). The scope line stays: GPU is Nx's. No ADR: the decision does not change.

Rules: one run each on a quiet machine, say so; no new measurement unless the owner asks (docs/agents/runs.md). No ticket ids in HexDocs. Done when: the entries are in, mix defk.docs --check passes.

title: Record the handwired study's speed lessons in docs/performance.md and the GPU evidence in docs/scope.md
